title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not by Grothendieck. It is page 5 of a typescript of Robert Steinberg's 'Regular elements of semisimple algebraic groups' (Publ. Math. IHÉS 25, 1965). It sits in the archive file among Grothendieck's handwritten 1965 notes on motives. The sheet is scanned upside down, consistent with a preprint whose blank backs Grothendieck used as scratch paper. The neighbouring pages are his handwritten notes on elements λ of CM fields with λ·λ̄ = q^i, i.e. Weil q-numbers, Frobenius eigenvalues and S-units.

Content of the page:
- Setting. G is a semisimple group over an algebraically closed field K. Earlier sections built a set N (1.4): for simply connected G, a cross-section of the regular conjugacy classes, built from a maximal torus T and simple reflections σ_i (the Steinberg cross-section).
- Perfect field. Steinberg now takes a perfect subfield k of K. He remarks that recent results of A. Grothendieck on semisimple groups over arbitrary fields (SGA 3, 1962–64) suggest perfectness is mostly unnecessary.
- Theorem 1.6. If G is defined over k and either splits over k, or is quasi-split (has a k-Borel subgroup) with no component of type A_n, n even, then N can be chosen defined over k. Consequently, for simply connected G, every k-rational regular class contains a k-rational element.
- Theorem 1.7 (Steinberg's rationality theorem). If G is simply connected and quasi-split over k, every semisimple conjugacy class defined over k contains a k-point. A substitute argument (9.7) handles type A_{2m}.
- Necessity. Sections 9.1 and 9.10 show the k-Borel hypothesis cannot be dropped.
errors: No mathematical errors on the page. It states known theorems of Steinberg, proved in his §9.

ideas.what: Rational cross-section of regular classes (Theorem 1.6) for split or quasi-split groups, excluding type A_{2m}
ideas.modern_name: Steinberg cross-section / Steinberg section defined over k

ideas.what: Every k-rational semisimple class of a simply connected quasi-split group contains a k-rational element (Theorem 1.7)
ideas.modern_name: Steinberg's theorem on rational conjugacy classes (used e.g. by Kottwitz)

ideas.what: Mention that Grothendieck's results on reductive groups over arbitrary fields remove the perfectness hypothesis
ideas.modern_name: SGA 3 theory of reductive group schemes (e.g. existence of maximal tori over any field)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript of Steinberg's published 1965 IHÉS paper, apparently reused as scratch paper for Grothendieck's motive notes. Its only Grothendieck content is the citation of SGA 3, which is well known. Archivally it is mildly interesting that Grothendieck had Steinberg's preprint in 1965, but there is nothing new mathematically.
transcription_corrections: The transcription is accurate. Note that the page image is upside down: it is the reverse of a scratch sheet, a typescript of Steinberg's 'Regular elements of semisimple algebraic groups', not a text by Grothendieck.
